Convergence and loss

Best objective, best feasible cost, penalty and cumulative decoder evaluations over the PSO iterations.

Vehicle-day timeline

Each bar is one trip; trips are shown sequentially in solution order. Each bar is one trip. Everything after the 8-hour shift is overtime at 2x. The last customer must be served by the last-delivery line; after it only the drive back is allowed, until the hard end of the day. Triangles mark each vehicle's last delivery.

Cost breakdown

Fuel, maintenance and base wages per vehicle, plus the vehicle-day overtime premium and the total cost composition.

Capacity and trip size

Weight and usable-volume utilisation per trip, and the number of customers per trip against the soft minimum of 10 and maximum of 50.

Route map and trip cost

Routes are drawn depot to customers and back. The scatter plot uses the standalone trip cost; the solution total adds vehicle-day overtime once.

The HTML report embeds the charts, so it can be opened without the PNG files. The CSV files are provided for further analysis in Excel or Python.

Reading notes

  • The convergence chart is the PSO loss curve: lower is better.
  • The timeline assumes trips are performed sequentially in solution order; it is a workload view, not a clock schedule.
  • The route map uses the latitude/longitude in locations.csv.
  • The solution is a heuristic result, not a certified global optimum.
